title: Normalize a league
prompt: Implement `normalize(weights)` for a dictionary of nonnegative numbers with positive total. Raise ValueError otherwise. Example: {'a':2,'b':1} gives probabilities 2/3 and 1/3.
hint: Check individual weights before dividing by their sum.

title: Population-weighted score
prompt: Implement `weighted_score(scores,weights)` with matching names and weights already summing to one. Example: scores .8,.4 with weights .25,.75 gives .5.
tests:
assert abs(weighted_score({'hog':.8,'siege':.4},{'hog':.25,'siege':.75})-.5)<1e-9, 'Use weights, not an unweighted mean'
assert weighted_score({'hog':.7},{'hog':1})==.7, 'One opponent keeps its score'
solution:
def weighted_score(scores,weights):
    return sum(scores[name]*w for name,w in weights.items())

title: Do not hide a weak matchup
prompt: Implement `passes(scores,mean_bar,min_bar)` requiring a nonempty list, mean >= mean_bar and every score >= min_bar. Example: [.8,.2],.5,.3 fails.
tests:
assert not passes([.8,.2],.5,.3), 'A weak subgroup must fail despite a passing mean'
assert passes([.6,.5],.55,.5), 'Meeting both inclusive thresholds passes'
assert not passes([],.5,.3), 'No evaluation evidence cannot pass'
hint: Check the empty list before computing a mean.
solution:
def passes(scores,mean_bar,min_bar):
    return bool(scores) and sum(scores)/len(scores)>=mean_bar and min(scores)>=min_bar

title: Name the winning seat
prompt: Implement `seat_rates(bot_wins,total)` for decisive no-draw counts. Return {'bot': rate, 'opponent': rate}; for total zero return both None. Example: 3/4 gives .75 and .25.
tests:
assert seat_rates(3,4)=={'bot':.75,'opponent':.25}, 'Opponent wins are the complement only in this no-draw fixture'
assert seat_rates(0,0)=={'bot':None,'opponent':None}, 'No games is not a zero-percent estimate'
assert seat_rates(0,5)['opponent']==1, 'All bot losses are opponent wins here'
